spec.title: Temperature explains about 15% of yearly forest water loss after wildfires
spec.statement: Bond-Lamberty et al. (Global Change Biology, 2009) studied water loss from Canadian boreal forests after fire. Their regression of yearly evapotranspiration on average temperature has an R-squared of 0.1495, as recorded in the author's 2008 output file. This re-runs the author's own original script, unchanged, on the published data.

source.authors: B. Bond-Lamberty, S. D. Peckham, S. T. Gower, B. E. Ewers

metric.name: R-squared of evapotranspiration on average temperature
